shorts.description:
There’s a lot of money left on the table by people selling subscriptions instead of bulk.

I’ll buy a year up front in bulk (especially at a discount) instead of a subscription.

shorts.description:
Growth hack: word your problems as personal deficiencies.

“My sales people suck” VS 
“I don’t know how to hire train and manage great salespeople.”

If you can improve it, it’s a skill.
If it’s a skill, you can learn it.

But you have to admit you suck before it can get better.

shorts.description:
Six years ago I was selling supplements at my gym and I ran out of inventory on a few key products.

I still had about 20 more consults left that day. And - I still needed to make money.

Result: I ended up selling more than I did when I was fully stocked & learned key lesson…

Same people ask what they need to do differently with their content.

I feel like I can consolidate all my dating advice into this:

Become worthy of the caliber of partner you want. 

Then, meet as many people as you can to find them. 

Ignore the rest.
shorts.title: Stop Comparing Your Chapter 1 to Someone's Chapter 10

shorts.description:
You don’t decrease churn.

You increase activation and consumption. 

Then churn decreases as a result.

Inputs vs outputs.
shorts.title: How to Get Clients to Stay Past 6 Months

shorts.description:
Building a brand seems complicated. Here’s my layman .02:

1) What you’ve done
2) What you say you’re gonna do that comes true (at a micro and macro level)
3) Other institutions/people you associate with (directly and indirectly)
4) Keeping 1-2-3 aligned with values you hold.
shorts.title: We're Switching From the Attention Economy to the Trust Economy

shorts.description: Entrepreneurship is an unending process of trading your time for increasingly valuable activities. The myth is that you will get to a point where you no longer are needed, but if you continue to grow as your company does, you will become more valuable, not less.
shorts.title: How to Know When to Hire Your First Employee

shorts.description:
Dairy Queen has ~4300 locations and $3B+ in annual revenue.

They were founded in 1940.

So it’s taken them 83 years to build this massive simple business empire.

A reminder that shit takes time.

shorts.description:
Just spend the time it takes to make an actually amazing product. (Way longer than normal). 

Then - right when you’d feel the most convicted about charging for it…

…give it away. 

And you get leads forever. 

Which is probably worth more than what you’d make from the thing.

shorts.description:
Sometimes it really is as simple as:

Double your leads. 
Double your business.
shorts.title: You Have 4x ROAS. Just Spend More.

shorts.description:
I believe the hardest decision in entrepreneurship is knowing when to give up.

The question is whether the lack of desired success is due to impatience, poor execution, or an opportunity not worth pursuing. 

Imo it’s the decision that requires the most discernment in the game.
shorts.title: Push or Pivot? How to Know the Difference

shorts.description: Sometimes you have to let your parents’ dream die for yours to live.

shorts.description:
If you've been thinking about starting a business for more than 6 months, stop.

Just offer to do something. Anything. For someone else. In exchange for money. Today.

And when you do, congrats, you own a business. 

Now you just gotta do more and better until the day you die.
shorts.title: What Business Can't Get to $100K/Month?

shorts.description: A lot of making a plan work comes down to sticking with the plan you originally started with without thinking things have changed when all they did was get hard.
shorts.title: The Fact That You're Uncomfortable Is Why You Should Persist

shorts.description:
If your business isn't making $100,000 a month. 
Follow these 2 steps. 
1) Grab a kitchen timer & turn it to 4 hours.
2) Advertise until the timer is up.

You can do warm outbound, cold outbound, content, or paid ads. Don’t do all of them. Just pick 1 until you get to $100k a month. I would start with outbound or content because they’re the cheapest to get started (aka free).

When the 4-hour timer is up, and the day is done - do it again tomorrow.
shorts.title: Prove You Can Make $1 Before You Quit Your Job

shorts.description:
How to never compromise in a relationship:

Find someone who wants the same thing as you. You both get what you want, and it just so happens - to be the same thing.
shorts.title: 69% of Relationship Problems Are Unsolvable

shorts.description:
suck at something
work for free
lots of times
suck less
wait until people ask for free work and you can't take them on
now you have more demand than you have supply
begin to charge money
boot out free clients for paid
and offer to keep working for $
congrats. u hav business

shorts.description:
The best to place learn marketing for a specific platform from are agency owners.

They walk the walk. Rather than pay for outdated trainings, pay them more than their normal fee to teach you while they execute.

You get the speed of agency and long term benefits of coaching.
shorts.title: How to Learn From Vendors Without Them Knowing

shorts.description:
A lot of entrepreneurship comes down to being able to look an existential threat in the eyes with equal parts dread and enthusiasm. 

And going from “this is gonna end us” to “we can turn this into a win” as fast as possible.
shorts.title: A Bird Doesn't Land on a Branch Because It Trusts the Branch

shorts.description:
In a capitalist system, both parties say thank you in an exchange. 

It’s one of the beautiful things about voluntary trade. 

Both parties see a net gain.

The best games are not zero sum.
shorts.title: To Argue Against Private Equity Is to Argue Against Capitalism

shorts.description:
The reason you’re confused about what opportunity to pursue is that your only goal is to make money. 

And since there are so many ways to do it, you can’t figure out which one to pick.

Fix: Figure out what you wanna DO. Then within that context, which version makes you money.
shorts.title: "I Quit My Job But Don't Know What Business to Start"

shorts.description:
The importance of betting big:

In entrepreneurship, you will lose more times than you win. So you just need to make sure that when you win, you win so big, it overshadows all your losses.

No one cares about small victories or defeats.
shorts.title: You're Playing $10 Blackjack as a Millionaire

shorts.description:
You can either do what’s convenient and become acceptable or you can do what’s required and become exceptional.

The second is painful for now. 
The first is painful forever.
shorts.title: Shame Is Breaking Other People's Rules, Guilt Is Breaking Your Own

shorts.description:
The most common constraint for business growth isn't access to capital but allocation of attention.

You don't need more money, you need fewer things to focus on.
shorts.title: Why You're Not Winning (You're Distracted)

shorts.description:
I didn’t want to make content for years because I didn’t want to make stuff that would disappear.

It felt pointless until I realized the content isn’t the output, the audience is.
shorts.title: Why I Was Wrong About Branding

shorts.description:
Have you ever thought…

 “I wish I could just fast forward thru this shitty part and get to when my goal becomes real?”

Right. Me too. 

But taken to the natural extreme, the day you die, you would’ve achieved all the goals you set out to accomplish. 

And then - immediately die. 

Which when you think about it - shows how silly it is for us to think this way. 

You might as well say “I’d like to fast forward to the end of the movie”

If that’s the case, you might as well not watch it. Or in our case - live it. 

So - the reverse of that would be to value the shitty part as equal (or even greater than) the end. 

Since we don’t want the story to end (we die), we flip the “fast forward to the end” frame to “slow down right now”

In other words - the todays - become the “good ol days” of our future selves looking back. 

And - doing the work - becomes the only goal worth living for.
shorts.title: At What Point Should You Enjoy the Fruits of Your Labor?

shorts.description:
Something that’s helped me post more:

Instead of: “How will my audience take this?’

I ask: “Would I post it anyways?”

And if so, I go for it. And your brand will adjust to reality. Which is endlessly more sustainable than an algorithm driven version of yourself you’ll never be
shorts.title: Good Content Beats Production Every Time

shorts.description:
A lot of management just comes down to:

Tell them what you want
Show them how to do it
Check in to make sure they did
Give feedback on the outcome

And just doing that until you die.
shorts.title: You're Asking Them to Guess and Somehow Get It Right

shorts.description:
Find what works. 
Do more of what works.
Find the thing preventing you from doing more of what works. 
Solve it.
Do more of what works.
Repeat.
shorts.title: Stop Judging Yourself for What's Actually Working

It doesn’t matter which one you pick. 

It just matters that you pick.

shorts.description:

Ignore the opinions of others. 
Do so much work it would be unreasonable that you fail.
Realize it never mattered to begin with.
Help others once you get there.

shorts.description:
One of the hardest business lessons I’ve had to learn is: you don’t try to get bigger.

Instead, you try and get better. 

The better you get, the bigger your customers will demand you become. 

Quality creates demand. 
Demand creates growth.

Not the other way around.
shorts.title: Your Business Isn't Failing Because of the Market

shorts.description:
If you're split between two paths, pick the one with the better story.
At the end of your life, it's all your gonna have left anyways.

shorts.description:
Easy model for business growth:

Give first. 
Don’t trade. 
Give. 
To lots of people. 
For free. 
Without asking for anything.
Keep going until someone wants more. Then you’re good enough to charge. 
Until then. 
Keep giving and getting better.

shorts.description:

…And no one likes a boring success story.

shorts.description:
My super productive day formula:

1) Remove all apps (this is the hardest & most effective - social, slack, phone call, sms, I mean everything)
2) Cover windows/visual distractions 
3) Wear ear plugs + ear muffs
4) Remove meetings
5) Stimulate (caffeine, nicotine, + your faves)
6) Set a timer per task
7) Rack em & stack em

Once you remove everything, all that’s left is the work.

And the best part is: removing stuff is free.
shorts.title: You Don't Lack Focus, You're Focusing on the Wrong Things
